listed the .NET forms that got no verdict. Each one is now either judged or recorded as out of scope, with the reason:

Framework is supported as part of Windows, so each version follows the lifecycle of the Windows releases it ships with, not the .NET release policy that every rule here cites. A rule needs an authoritative Microsoft lifecycle source per version and a statement of which Windows releases it assumes; the releases index the
importer reads has no Framework data. Judging it from the .NET policy would be a guess. A future decision may add a Framework rule set with its own source.
Properties are unclassified; imported and conditional values are skipped.
